newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Deve Gowda leaves for Davos forum.
newsitem.headline: India's Deve Gowda leaves for Davos forum.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda left for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland on Friday morning, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
On his week-long trip, Deve Gowda was set to attend the Davos forum before leaving for Mauritius next Monday. He was due to return to the capital on the morning of February 6.
Shares on the Bombay Stock Exchange opened sharply lower on Friday as traders sold after their expectations of a package of government measures failed to materialise.
At 10:30 a.m. (0500 GMT), the Bombay exchange's sensitive index was down 66.60 points, or 1.90 percent, to 3,443.45.

Stock prices had broadly risen in January after Deve Gowda said measures to spur capital markets and stimulate economic growth would be announced before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram left for Davos.
Chidambaram said on Thursday that decisions already taken this month by the government to spur the economy amounted to a package of economic reforms.
"Taken together, I believe, they constitute a cohesive package of decisions which will impart greater thrust to economic reforms," Chidambaram said in a statement.
